571.canonical: Expect a cognitive strategy itself to be structurally simple — underline main ideas, divide the problem into parts — with correspondingly simple, well-known prerequisites that get simpler the more general the strategy, while requiring that the prior knowledge it operates on be readily retrievable, since a schema is what supplies the strategy's retrieval cues; even young children respond to a suggested strategy.

580.canonical: Arrange the external conditions for attitude modelling as a four-step sequence — present the model and establish its appeal and credibility, have the learner recall knowledge of the situations the attitude applies to, have the model communicate or demonstrate the desired choice of personal action, and show the model obtaining pleasure or satisfaction from the outcome — since without the learner observing both the choice and its vicarious reinforcement the modelling does not establish the attitude.
